documents.title: Full duty note
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Morning. Burn clinic said full duty starting January. My insurance carrier for the business wants something in writing from a doctor before they close out the disability claim. Can you send a letter? Legs feel good, I'm plowing for a couple of commercial lots this winter.

documents.title: Return to work letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Connor Warner may return to full duty without restrictions as of January 5, 2026, consistent with the recommendation of his burn surgery team. Please contact the office with any questions.

documents.title: Spot on my arm
documents.author: patient
documents.body: You told me to tell you if a spot changed. There's a mole on my left forearm I first noticed in the spring. It's gotten bigger and darker the last month or so. Doesn't hurt or bleed. Given my dad I'd rather not sit on it.

documents.title: RE: Spot on my arm
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad you wrote. Let's look at it this week. Front desk will call you in the morning with a time, Wednesday if that works.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

orders.reason: changing pigmented lesion left forearm, father with melanoma

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here for a spot on the left forearm. First noticed it a few months ago, maybe March. Over the past several weeks it has gotten larger and the color has changed, darker in parts. No itching, bleeding or pain. Works outside all season, sunscreen inconsistent. Father died of melanoma.

Healthy otherwise, legs doing well, back to full work since January. Meds none, NKDA.

Exam: pigmented lesion dorsal left forearm, irregular in outline and color, larger than the nearby freckles. No other worrisome lesions on a quick look at arms, back and legs; grafted lower legs healed. No palpable left axillary or epitrochlear nodes.

A/P: changing pigmented lesion, left forearm, concerning given evolution and family history. Urgent dermatology referral for evaluation and biopsy; asked the referral coordinator to push for a slot within a few weeks. He will message if it bleeds or changes further before then.

documents.title: Dermatology consultation (received)
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology group. Visit 07/29/2026.
Thank you for referring Mr. Warner, a 41-year-old landscaper, for a pigmented lesion of the left forearm. This is his first visit with us. He first saw the spot several months ago; lately it has enlarged and its color has changed. About a year ago he was treated for full-thickness leg burns from a house fire, with fasciotomies and grafting, now healed.
Family history: father with melanoma diagnosed at 55, deceased; paternal uncle with basal cell carcinoma; mother with type 2 diabetes.
Social: long hours of sun exposure at work. Never smoker.
Medications: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: on the dorsal left forearm there is an 8 mm pigmented lesion with an irregular border and variegated brown-black color. Dermoscopy shows an irregular pigment network with atypical dots and globules. The remainder of the full-skin exam shows scattered benign-appearing nevi and solar lentigines; healed grafts on both lower legs.
Assessment: atypical pigmented lesion of the left forearm, melanoma must be excluded.
Procedure: excisional biopsy with narrow margins performed today after consent, under local anesthesia, closed with sutures. Specimen to dermatopathology.
Plan: pathology pending; we will contact him with results and next steps. Suture removal in 10 to 14 days.
Dermatology attending

conditions.label: Malignant melanoma of left upper limb, including shoulder
conditions.note: left forearm, superficial spreading, 1.2 mm, pT2a

reports.text:
Specimen: skin, left dorsal forearm, excisional biopsy.
Gross: ellipse of skin 1.6 x 0.8 cm with a central irregular pigmented lesion, 0.8 cm.
Microscopic: invasive malignant melanoma, superficial spreading type. Tumor thickness 1.2 mm. Ulceration absent. Mitotic rate 2 per mm2. No lymphovascular or perineural invasion identified. No microsatellites. Peripheral margin involved by melanoma in situ at one edge; deep margin free of invasive melanoma.
reports.conclusion: Invasive malignant melanoma, superficial spreading type, left forearm, 1.2 mm thick, nonulcerated, pT2a. Peripheral margin involved by melanoma in situ.

documents.title: Dermatology note: pathology result (received)
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body: Called Mr. Warner with pathology: invasive melanoma of the left forearm, 1.2 mm, nonulcerated, pT2a. Explained that this thickness calls for wider excision and sentinel lymph node biopsy. Referred to surgical oncology, appointment 08/10. Copy to PCP.

documents.title: Call to patient re: pathology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Saw the derm path come in. Called Connor. He'd already heard from dermatology and has surgical oncology Monday. Understandably shaken, thinking about his dad. Went over that this was caught at a thin stage, no ulceration, and the next step is wider excision plus checking the first lymph node. Answered questions about work: fine to keep working until surgery, long sleeves and sunscreen. He has my number.

documents.title: Surgical oncology consultation (received)
documents.author: surgical oncology
documents.body:
Dear Doctor,
Mr. Warner is a healthy 41-year-old man seen 08/10/2026 for a newly diagnosed melanoma of the left forearm, superficial spreading type, 1.2 mm thick, nonulcerated, mitotic rate 2/mm2, pT2a, excised by dermatology on 07/29 with melanoma in situ at one peripheral edge. No symptoms. Past history notable for bilateral leg burns in 2025 treated with escharotomies, fasciotomies and grafting. Father had melanoma. No medications. NKDA.
Exam: healing biopsy scar on the dorsal left forearm, no satellite or in-transit lesions. No palpable left epitrochlear, axillary or cervical nodes. Rest of the exam unremarkable.
Plan: wide local excision with 1 to 2 cm margins and sentinel lymph node biopsy with preoperative lymphoscintigraphy, scheduled 08/19. No staging imaging is needed for this stage. Risks and recovery reviewed; he can expect a week off heavy work.
Surgical oncology attending

events.reason: Wide local excision and sentinel lymph node biopsy

documents.title: Operative report: wide local excision and sentinel node biopsy (received)
documents.author: surgical oncology
documents.body:
Date of surgery 08/19/2026, outpatient surgery center of a regional hospital.
Diagnosis: melanoma of the left forearm, pT2a, status post excisional biopsy.
Procedures: wide local excision of the left forearm melanoma site with 1.5 cm margins and layered closure; left axillary sentinel lymph node biopsy.
Lymphoscintigraphy this morning showed drainage to the left axilla. Two hot and blue sentinel nodes removed through a small axillary incision; background count low after removal. No clinically suspicious nodes. Specimens to pathology.
Anesthesia: general. EBL minimal. No complications. Discharged home the same day with acetaminophen and ibuprofen as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.

reports.text:
A. Skin and subcutaneous tissue, left forearm, wide local excision: healing biopsy site with scar; no residual melanoma in situ or invasive melanoma. Margins clear.
B. Lymph node, left axillary sentinel #1: one lymph node, negative for melanoma by H&E and immunohistochemistry (0/1).
C. Lymph node, left axillary sentinel #2: one lymph node, negative for melanoma by H&E and immunohistochemistry (0/1).
reports.conclusion: No residual melanoma; margins clear. Sentinel lymph nodes negative for metastatic melanoma (0/2).

documents.title: Surgical oncology letter: final pathology (received)
documents.author: surgical oncology
documents.body:
Dear Doctor,
Final pathology from Mr. Warner's surgery on 08/19 shows no residual melanoma with clear margins, and both left axillary sentinel nodes are negative (0/2). His final stage is IB (pT2a N0 M0).
Recommendations: no adjuvant therapy and no routine surveillance imaging. Full-skin examinations with dermatology every 3 to 6 months for the first two years, then less often; monthly self skin checks; daily sun protection, which matters for his work. Wound check with us next week. He knows to report any new lump in the arm or armpit.
Medications: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Surgical oncology attending

documents.title: Surgery results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted you to hear it from me too, the lymph nodes were clean and they got it all. Arm is sore but fine. How soon can I get back on a mower? Surgeon said a week for heavy stuff but I forgot to ask about the vibration on the arm.

documents.title: RE: Surgery results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's the result we were hoping for, really glad. Ask the surgeon at your wound check next week, they'll want to see how the incision looks before you put that arm to work. Until then light use only. Keep the dermatology skin checks on the calendar, and I'll see you for your physical in November.
